images.title: 29 notches read as fives
images.purpose: Shows the 29 notches of the old tally bone grouped into 5 groups of five and 4 more.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One long pale bone shape across the middle of the frame with notches cut along it, brackets underneath each group.
images.exact_structure: One long horizontal bone shape (pale cream fill, dark outline, rounded knobbed ends). Along its top edge, exactly 29 short vertical dark notches, arranged as 5 clusters of 5 notches followed by 1 cluster of 4 notches, with a clear gap between clusters. Under each of the 5 clusters of five, one amber (#E69F00) bracket labelled 5. Under the cluster of four, one teal (#0072B2) bracket labelled 4. Above the bone, centred, the label 29 notches. Exactly 6 brackets. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Grouping tally marks in fives makes 29 easy to read: five fives and 4 more.
images.description: Shows the 29 notches of the old tally bone grouped into 5 groups of five and 4 more.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the 29 marks bunched into fives shows why grouping helps the eye.
